description: Schedule Timeline Grid (Rooms-as-Rows Rewrite) — replace the column-per-room desktop grid and single-room mobile calendar with one responsive timeline grid (rooms as rows, time as a horizontal axis) that scales to 30 rooms, preserving drag-to-create, pin/favorite, hide-free-rooms, building groups, keyboard navigation, and the now-line. Source: tasks/prd-schedule-timeline-grid.md.

userStories.title: Horizontal time-axis math utilities
userStories.description: As a developer, I need percentage-based time-to-position conversion functions (the horizontal-axis equivalent of the existing pixel-based offsetForTime/timeForOffset in lib/schedule/hours.ts) so every component that positions something along the time axis shares one implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: percentForTime(time) returns 0 at SCHEDULE_START_HOUR and 100 at SCHEDULE_END_HOUR (existing constants: 8 and 23), clamped for times outside that range
timeForPercent(percent) is the inverse, snapped to BOOKING_TIME_STEP_MINUTES the same way the existing timeForOffset is
A gridline helper returns hour and half-hour marks as percentages across the operating window, for the time header and background gridlines to share
Existing vertical offsetForTime/timeForOffset stay in place untouched until US-012 removes them, so nothing else in the app breaks mid-refactor
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added percentForTime/timeForPercent/timeAxisGridlines to lib/schedule/hours.ts alongside the untouched vertical offsetForTime/timeForOffset. Added lib/schedule/hours.test.ts (11 tests). Also added resolve.alias for "@" to vitest.config.ts since hours.ts's pre-existing "@/lib/dates" import wasn't resolvable under vitest before this story's test file exercised it.

userStories.notes: Renamed useNowOffsetPx to useNowOffsetPercent in lib/schedule/now-line.ts (now uses US-001's percentForTime, same 60s refresh/null-unless-today logic). NowLine now renders a vertical border-l-2 line at left:X% spanning inset-y-0 with the dot repositioned to the top-left, replacing the old horizontal border-t-2/top-offset line. Typecheck and lint pass; verified against the real dev server (linked remote Supabase) with a temp Playwright-driven test user/seeded booking — confirmed the rendered style is left:<percent>% matching percentForTime math exactly, and that it disappears when navigating to a different date.

userStories.title: Horizontal event block
userStories.description: As a member scanning the schedule, I want each booking rendered as a horizontal block positioned by time, showing as much detail as its width allows.
acceptanceCriteria: EventBlock positions itself by left/width percentages (via US-001) instead of the current top/height + column-based left/width; top/height become its lane position within the room row (for concurrent-overlap stacking, see US-005)
At rendered width >=90px: title/service, time range, and requester name all show (existing priority order)
Between 40-90px: title only, truncated with ellipsis
Below 40px: no text at all, just the colored block; hovering/focusing shows the existing kit Tooltip with the full title, time range, and requester
DragCreateOverlay is updated to the same left/width horizontal positioning, keeping its existing pending/conflict styling
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: EventBlock now positions left/width via percentForTime(startTime/endTime) instead of column-based left/width; top/height are now caller-supplied lane position (px). Rendered width is measured via ResizeObserver (border-box) and drives 3 density tiers: >=90px full (time/service/requester, unchanged), 40-89px title-only (service, falling back to time label) truncated, <40px no text (existing hover/focus Popover still shows full details regardless of tier). DragCreateOverlay now takes left/width percent props (from percentForTime) instead of top/height. Updated the two old call sites (desktop-resource-grid.tsx, mobile-day-calendar.tsx) to match the new prop contracts so the app still compiles/runs; per this PRD's established precedent (US-002 already made NowLine vertical in these same soon-to-be-deleted components), their old vertical-time visual correctness is not preserved mid-refactor - they're replaced wholesale by TimelineGrid in US-004/US-005/US-012. Typecheck, lint, and vitest (53 tests) pass. Verified in a real browser against the linked remote Supabase (temp signed-up test user + seeded booking, cleaned up after): confirmed EventBlock renders without crashing, computed time labels are correct, and forcing the block's rendered width through 200/70/60/45/20px confirmed the three density tiers exactly at the 90/40px boundaries; hover on a collapsed block still showed the full popover; a mouse drag produced a correctly time-labeled ghost overlay via the new left/width props with no console errors.

userStories.title: TimelineGrid skeleton — sticky room column, sticky time header
userStories.description: As a member on any device, I want one calendar component (not a separate mobile/desktop pair) with a room column that stays visible on the left and a time header that stays visible at the top while I scroll.
acceptanceCriteria: New components/schedule/timeline-grid.tsx, built mobile-first and responsive, not yet wired with real bookings (structural shell only for this story)
Room column is position: sticky; left: 0; each cell shows room name, "cap. N" as secondary text (nothing if capacity is null), and a thin colored left bar using the room's existing category_color
Frozen column width: 140px at >=1024px, 100px between 768-1023px, ~88px below 768px

Time header is position: sticky; top: 0 inside the scroll container; hour labels every 1 hour when the container is >=1100px wide, every 2 hours below that; vertical hairline gridlines at each hour, a lighter half-hour gridline when the rendered per-hour width has room for one
Renders correctly with a temporary 30-room fixture (removed after verification) without layout breaking
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Added components/schedule/timeline-grid.tsx: a flexbox-based (not CSS grid) rooms-as-rows shell with a sticky room column (left:0, w-[88px]/md:100px/lg:140px, colored category_color bar + name + "cap. N") and a sticky time header (top:0) inside a max-h-[70vh] overflow-auto pane so the sticky positioning has a real internal scroll container to stick within (bare overflow-auto with no bound height doesn't scroll, so sticky is a no-op against it - verified this the hard way with a real browser check before adding the max-height). Hour labels/gridlines reuse US-001's timeAxisGridlines; label density switches 1hr/2hr at a measured (ResizeObserver) axis width of 1100px, half-hour gridlines show once per-hour width >=48px, and the axis has a min-width of 560px so 2-hour-step labels never collide on narrow phones (verified overlapping pixel rects at 420px before raising it) - forcing native horizontal scroll on mobile, which anticipates US-008. Added category_color to ScheduleRoom (lib/rooms-filters.ts) and the schedule page's room query select. Typecheck, lint, and npm test (53 tests) pass. Verified in the real dev server (linked remote Supabase, temp admin-API-created test user, deleted after) via a temporary 30-room fixture page (deleted after verification): confirmed responsive column widths at 390/800/1400px, confirmed the header and room column genuinely stay pinned during both vertical (internal pane) and horizontal (mobile, axis min-width forces scroll) scrolling, confirmed hour-label density and half-hour-gridline thresholds switch at the right measured widths, and caught/fixed two real rendering bugs along the way (sticky header not sticking without a bounded scroll container; hour-label text clipping/colliding at narrow widths).
